chunks.l2:
[tal-a04-v01] Now we declare the circle of shakti means for supreme self-knowledge.

[tal-a04-v10] But the supreme lord, pure through difficult doing and free will, is skilled in the play of concealing himself.

[tal-a04-v02] In that supreme lordly nature, one desiring entry into distinction should refine it directly.

[tal-a04-v03] Refined distinction produces a self-refined distinction equal to itself, and that produces another similar one.

[tal-a04-v04] In four distinctions, refinement gradually moves from unclear to becoming clear and fully clear-natured.

[tal-a04-v05] Then it becomes clearer until the clearest; even from the unclear beginning, difference remains between stages.

[tal-a04-v06] Then consciousness, filled with the clearest nobility of form, approaches pure non-distinct nature.

[tal-a04-v07] Therefore, for those reflecting again and again, the clear selfhood of that consciousness-natured radiance arises.

[tal-a04-v08] But how can consciousness, supreme knower made of reflection, reflect by itself in such creation without becoming inert?

[tal-a04-v09] It is said that self-consciousness is full by nature alone; nothing is to be removed or added, as said before.

chunks.l2:
[tal-a04-v11] Even when his own form is uncovered, the lord's self-concealment is maya, because difference occurs throughout the world.

[tal-a04-v12] Such appearance of the great lord is called duality; by removing that duality, this is called reflection.

[tal-a04-v13] The wise cut the root of this hard-to-split tree with the axe of true logic; this is certain.

[tal-a04-v14] The wise call that meditation all-desire-milking; it clarifies things and removes even what rests in the mind.

[tal-a04-v15] In the prior scripture logic is stated to be the best limb of yoga, and effort is praised for considering what should be rejected.

[tal-a04-v16] When the mind is steadied on the path, even desire for objects impels it; by that it should be led until the diseaseless state.

[tal-a04-v17] The path here is a means of liberation, but that path taught elsewhere is rejectable because desire pervades and binds what is joined with necessity.

[tal-a04-v18] The principle of attachment, as stated by that, makes one attached there, just as seeing royal enjoyment, unseen obstruction, leads to attachment.

[tal-a04-v19] One may be attached in enjoyment, even in liberation like the evil-minded; that portion is called nature, and this is clearly said.

[tal-a04-v20] The wise say that what is called an accomplishment limb is an obstacle to liberation, even for those who know the greatness of Shiva's teaching.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-anāvṛtte svarūpe@pi yadātmācchādanaṃ vibhoḥ / saiva māyā yato bheda etāvānviśvavṛttikaḥ tathābhāsanamevāsya dvaitamuktaṃ maheśituḥ / taddvayāpāsanenāyaṃ parāmarśo@bhidhīyate durbhedapādapasyāsya mūlaṃ kṛntanti kovidāḥ / dhārārūḍhena sattarkakuṭhāreṇeti niścayaḥ tāmenāṃ bhāvanāmāhuḥ sarvakāmadughāṃ budhāḥ / sphuṭayedvastu yāpetaṃ manosthapadādapi śrīpūrvaśāstre tatproktaṃ tarko yogāṅgamuttamam / heyādyālocanāttasmāttatra yatnaḥ praśasyate mārge cetaḥ sthirībhūtaṃ heye@pi viṣayecchayā / prerya tena nayettāvadyāvatpadamanāmayam mārgo@tra mokṣopāyaḥ sa heyaḥ śāstrāntaroditaḥ / viṣiṇoti nibadhnāti yecchā niyatisaṃgatam rāgatattvaṃ tayoktaṃ yat tena tatrānurajyate / yathā sāmrājyasaṃbhogaṃ dṛṣṭvādṛṣṭvāthabādhame bhoge rajyeta durbuddhistadvanmokṣe@pi rāgataḥ / sa evāṃśaka ityuktaḥ svabhāvākhyaḥ sa tu sphuṭam siddhyaṅgamiti mokṣāya pratyūha iti kovidāḥ / śivaśāsanamāhātmyaṃ vidannapyata eva hi

chunks.l2:
[tal-a04-v21] A fool may be attached in Vaishnava teachings, colored by attachment, because that is his divine power called Vama.

[tal-a04-v22] Some foolish ones are seen blaming royal enjoyment, and this expands from Pañcaratra, Brahma, and Buddhist traditions.

[tal-a04-v23] Not from contentment, but from desire proceeding in their own enjoyments, minds become intent on blaming Bhairava possession.

[tal-a04-v24] They become fallen by very terrible powers; therefore, even knowers in other teachings should know the greatness of the Shaiva teaching.

[tal-a04-v25] Having been reassured, one should not cross from the great ocean of difference; this is clearly stated in the Śrīkāmikā and in the section on bonds.

[tal-a04-v26] Those wise seers who know Veda, Sāṃkhya, and Purāṇas, devoted to Pāñcarātra, and devoted to other scriptures.

[tal-a04-v27] All Buddhists, Arhats, and others are colored by attachment to knowledge; because they are bound by the Māyā bond, they do not obtain Śiva initiation.

[tal-a04-v28] By the word rāga is stated the rāga principle as regulator in Māyā; and that regulates him in that scripture.

[tal-a04-v29] Even the liberation of Vaiṣṇavas and others is imagined by their own resolve: union with higher nature, or bliss-form.

[tal-a04-v30] Or only purified mind, or lamp-like cessation of continuum; that is composed of dissolution of knowable and unknowable self into kalā.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-vaiṣṇavādhyeṣu rajyeta mūḍho rāgeṇa rañjitaḥ / yatastāvati sā tasya vāmākhyā śaktiraiśvarī pāñcarātrikavairiñcasaugatādervijṛmbhate / dṛṣṭāḥ sāmrājyasaṃbhogaṃ nindantaḥ ke@pi vāliśāḥ na tu saṃtoṣataḥ sveṣu bhogeṣvāśīḥpravartanāt / evaṃcidbhairavāveśanindātatparamānasāḥ bhavantyatisughorābhiḥ śaktibhiḥ pātitā yataḥ / tena śāṃbhavamāhātmyaṃ jānanyaḥ śāsanāntare āśvasto nottarītavyaṃ tena bhedamahārṇavāt / śrīkāmikāyāṃ proktaṃ ca pāśaprakaraṇe sphuṭam vedasāṃkhyapurāṇajñāḥ pāñcarātraparāyaṇāḥ / ye kecidṛṣayo dhīrāḥ śāstrāntaraparāyaṇāḥ bauddhārhatādyāḥ sarve te vidyārāgeṇa rañjitāḥ / māyāpāśena baddhatvācchivadīkṣāṃ na vindate rāgaśabdena ca proktaṃ rāgatattvaṃ niyāmakam / māyīye tacca taṃ tasmiñchāstre niyamayediti mokṣo@pi vaiṣṇavāderyaḥ svasaṃkalpena bhāvitaḥ / paraprakṛtisāyujyaṃ yadvāpyānandarūpatā viśuddhacittamātraṃ vā dīpavatsaṃtatikṣayaḥ / sa savedyāpavedyātmapralayākalatāmayaḥ

chunks.l2:
[tal-a04-v31] Having attained it, for a long time, consumed by that enjoyment; at the end of dissolution of that principle, then one goes to a higher creation.

[tal-a04-v32] It becomes mantra by awakening from Ananteśa's creation; we will explain this ahead; let that be for now here.

[tal-a04-v33] He who is mocked by doctrines fabricated by ignorant people, rooted in false guru, is colored by the Māyā bond.

[tal-a04-v34] He too, by union of right reasoning, is led toward the true guru; right reasoning is pure knowledge, and that is the will of the supreme lord.

[tal-a04-v35] In the Śrīpūrva scripture it is said by him: desiring, by Śiva's will, for accomplishment of enjoyment and liberation, one is led toward the true guru.

[tal-a04-v36] But grace there proceeds gradually, for one who, abiding in the true guru or in another scripture, has taken the right path.

[tal-a04-v37] Here, in the being guided by guru and scripture, the variety of descent of power is distinguished beforehand.

[tal-a04-v38] As said in the Svacchanda scripture, māyā deludes all teachers, even in liberation, through desire for liberation.

[tal-a04-v39] But one rooted there, skilled in reflection, is purified by descent of power through the glory of pure knowledge.

[tal-a04-v40] He ascends the true path free from obstacles, and his reasoning proceeds from himself.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-taṃ prāpyāpi ciraṃ kālaṃ tadgogābhogabhuktataḥ / tattattvapralayānte tu tadūrdhvāṃ sṛṣṭimāgataḥ mantratvameti saṃbodhādananteśena kalpitāt / etaccāgre taniṣyāma ityāstāṃ tāvadatra tat tenājñajanatāklṛptapravādairyo viḍambitaḥ / asadgurau rūḍhacitsa māyāpāśena rañjitaḥ so@pi sattarkayogena nīyate sadguruṃ prati / sattarkaḥ śuddhavidyaiva sā cecchā parameśituḥ śrīpūrvaśāstre tenoktaṃ sa yiyāsuḥ śivecchayā / bhuktimuktiprasiddhyarthaṃ nīyate sadguruṃ prati śaktipātastu tatraiṣa kramikaḥ saṃpravartate / sthitvā yo@sadgurau śāstrāntare vā satpathaṃ śritaḥ guruśāstragate sattve@sattve cātra vibhedakam / śaktipātasya vaicitryaṃ purastātpravivicyate uktaṃ svacchandaśāstre tat vaiṣṇavādyānpravādinaḥ / sarvānbhramayate māyā sāmokṣe moKṣalipsayā yastu rūḍho@pi tatrodyatparāmarśaviśāradaḥ / sa śuddhavidyāmāhātmyācchaktipātapavitritaḥ ārohatyeva sanmārgaṃ pratyūhaparivarjitaḥ / sa tāvatkasyacittarkaḥ svata eva pravartate

chunks.l2:
[tal-a04-v41] This innate, self-evident knowledge is declared in scripture; even in the Kiraṇa it is said to come from guru, scripture, and self.

[tal-a04-v42] There, increasingly primary means are the former means; one whose true reasoning arises from himself is entitled everywhere.

[tal-a04-v43] Consecrated and initiated by the goddesses of self-knowledge, he alone is proclaimed chief among all teachers.

[tal-a04-v44] In his presence, not in others, is authority; he understands all scripture meaning from true reasoning alone.

[tal-a04-v45] Pure knowledge is truth; if it does not illuminate, then his sudden knowing of all scripture meaning arises.

[tal-a04-v46] Thus in the previous sacred statement, from the word sudden, the reason not famous in the world is said to be why.

[tal-a04-v47] This is the expansion of pure knowledge of the supreme lord; its teachings are many, both without foundation and with foundation.

[tal-a04-v48] He, gone to all parts, is established in primary and secondary parts: foundation, dependence on others, supreme wisdom, and its making.

[tal-a04-v49] Whoever truly knows becomes an accomplished yogi and an initiated one.

[tal-a04-v50] Thus, for one who knows by truth, initiation leads to liberation, as declared in that holy treatise.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-sa ca sāṃsiddhikaḥ śāstre proktaḥ svapratyayātmakaḥ / kiraṇāyāṃ yadapyuktaṃ gurutaḥ śāstrataḥ svataḥ tatrottarottaraṃ mukhyaṃ pūrvapūrva upāyakaḥ / yasya svato@yaṃ sattarkaḥ sarvatraivādhikāravān abhiṣiktaḥ svasaṃvittidevībhirdīkṣitaśca saḥ / sa eva sarvācāryāṇāṃ madhye mukhyaḥ prakīrtitaḥ tatsaṃnidhāne nānyeṣu kalpiteṣvadhikāritā / sa samastaṃ ca śāstrārthaṃ sattarkādeva manyate śuddhavidyā hi tannāsti satyaṃ yadyanna bhāsayet / sarvaśāstrārthavettṛtvamakasmāccāsya jāyate iti śrīpūvavākye tad+akasmāditi-śabdataḥ / lokāprasiddho yo hetuḥ so@kasmāditi kathyate sa caiṣa parameśānaśuddhavidyāvijṛmbhatam / asya bhodāśca bahavo nirbhittiḥ sahabhittikaḥ sarvago@ṃśagataḥ so@pi mukhyāmukhyāṃśaniṣṭhitaḥ / bhittiḥ paropajīvitvaṃ parā prajñātha tatkṛtiḥ adṛṣṭamaṇḍalo@pyevaṃ yaḥ kaścidvetti tattvataḥ / sa siddhibhāgbhavennityaṃ sa yogī sa ca dīkṣitaḥ evaṃ yo vetti tattvena tasya nirvāṇagāminī / dīkṣā bhavediti proktaṃ tacchrītriṃśakaśāsane

chunks.l2:
[tal-a04-v51] The unimagined guru is known by knowledge and remembered as innate; one without meditation on that form lacks the supreme.

[tal-a04-v52] A scripture knower is called guru in scripture, declared as an imagined imaginer, and his distinctions arise by superior, medium, and inferior means.

[tal-a04-v53] From meditation, chanting, dream, vow, or offering, the great-minded one obtains unimagined great initiation.

[tal-a04-v54] This is in the holy Vajasaneya, Vira, and Brahmayamala, and is clearly declared elsewhere by the creator.

[tal-a04-v55] Due to self-will, his activity is accepted as infinite, sometimes through devotion yoga, action, or knowledge.

[tal-a04-v56] By teaching of knowledge and dharma, by mantras, initiation, and many similar means, the supreme lord acts.

[tal-a04-v57] The lord of the universe graces worldly beings, dear one, through mother-circle awakening and purification.

[tal-a04-v58] From meditation, yoga, chanting, knowledge, mantra worship, and vow, one obtains family-common knowledge that grants kaula accomplishment.

[tal-a04-v59] Wherever the goal consisting of truth-knowledge is seen, he indeed is guru there; let the network of causes be imagined.

[tal-a04-v60] Without truth-knowledge there is no other mark; this is declared in Brahmayamala when service is done without doubt.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-akalpito gururjñayaḥ sāṃsiddhika iti smṛtaḥ / yastu tadrūpabhāgātmabhāvanātaḥ paraṃ vinā śāstravitsa guruḥ śāstre prokto@kalpitakalpakaḥ / tasyāpi bhedā utkṛṣṭamadhyamandādyupāyataḥ bhāvanāto@tha vā dhyānājjapātsvapnādvratāddhuteḥ / prāpnotyakalpitodāramabhiṣekaṃ mahāmatiḥ śrīmadvājasanīye śrīvīre śrībrahmayāmale / śrīsiddhāyāmidaṃ dhātrā proktamanyatra ca sphuṭam tasya svecchāpravṛttatvātkāraṇānantateṣyate / kadācidbhaktiyogena karmaṇā vidyayāpi vā jñānadharmopadeśena mantrairvā dīkṣayāpi vā / evamādyairanekaiśca prakāraiḥ parameśvaraḥ saṃsāriṇo@nugṛhṇāti viśvasya jagataḥ patiḥ / mātṛmaṇḍalasaṃbodhātsaṃskārāttapasaḥ priye dhyānādyogājjapājjñānānmantrārādhanāto vratāt / saṃprāpyaṃ kulasāmānyaṃ jñānaṃ kaulikasiddhidam tattvajñānātmakaṃ sādhyaṃ yatra yatraiva dṛśyate / sa eva hi gurustatra hetujālaṃ prakalpyatām tattvajñānādṛte nānyallakṣaṇaṃ brahmayāmale / tatraiva coktaṃ sevāyāṃ kṛtāyāmavikalpataḥ

chunks.l2:
[tal-a04-v61] If the practitioner has no success, self-initiation is given through the naming sequence.

[tal-a04-v62] Then self-knowledge, establishing vividness, accomplishes what is to be accomplished.

[tal-a04-v63] If the primary teacher is not vivid, then again in the worship of red Tara.

[tal-a04-v64] Doing the declared rule always, the teacher is monthly, the practitioner is half-fortnight initiate, and so on.

[tal-a04-v65] When the teacher is unavailable, one should perform this declared rule by mantra practice of the red goddess from the sequence.

[tal-a04-v66] In opinion, in study from a book, such a fault is said; if that fault is absent, there is no prohibition.

[tal-a04-v67] When asked what fruit comes from secrecy of mantra and substances, book-learned knowledge belongs to those devoid of the initiation rite.

[tal-a04-v68] Dark-natured ones practice harm to others and subjugation enough, but they do not know truth; thus they are clearly fault-bearing.

[tal-a04-v69] First a pair of words is to be spoken mutually as cause and effect; but without scripture one does not attain pure-knowledge-named awareness.

[tal-a04-v70] He who seeks the scripture declared by the teacher should perform the sequence, having worshipped the teacher with devotion by any means.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-sādhakasya na cetsiddhiḥ kiṃ kāryamiti codite / ātmīyamasya saṃjñānakrameṇa svātmadīkṣaṇam sasphuratvaprasiddhyarthaṃ tataḥ sādhyaṃ prasiddhyati / anena svātmavijñānaṃ sasphuratvaprasādhakam uktaṃ mukhyatayācāryo bhavedyadi na sasphuraḥ / tatraiva ca punaḥ śrīmadraktārādhanakarmaṇi vidhiṃ proktaṃ sadā kurvanmāsenācārya ucyate / pakṣeṇa sādhako@rdhārdhātputrakaḥ samayī tathā dīkṣayejjapayogena raktādevī kramādyataḥ / guroralābhe proktasya vidhimetaṃ samācaret mate ca pustakādvidyādhyayane doṣa īdṛśaḥ / ukto yastena taddoṣābhāve@sau na niṣiddhatā mantradravyādiguptatve phalaṃ kimiti codite / pustakādhītavidyā ye dīkṣāsamayavarjitāḥ tāmasāḥ parahiṃsādi vaśyādi ca carantyalam / na ca tattvaṃ vidustena doṣabhāja iti sphuṭam pūrvaṃ padayugaṃ vācyamanyonyaṃ hetuhetumat / yastu śāstraṃ vinā naiti śuddhavidyākhyasaṃvidam guroḥ sa śāstramanvicchustaduktaṃ kramamācaret / yena kenāpyupāyena gurumārādhya bhaktitaḥ

chunks.l2:
[tal-a04-v71] By that initiation sequence he knows the meaning of scripture; then, having obtained consecration, he becomes appointed.

[tal-a04-v72] Skilled in removing all bonds, he acts by proper sequence in some scriptural matter.

[tal-a04-v73] Sudden awakening occurs; among imagined and unimagined parts, the unimagined part is remembered as most excellent.

[tal-a04-v74] Excellence arises from degrees of pure knowledge, as difference begins from accomplished Shiva and liberated Shiva is below.

[tal-a04-v75] Thus lower possessors of acquired knowledge have no authority in its presence, like liberated Shiva self.

[tal-a04-v76] But silent standing or action remains; following that is duty, and even unimagined form makes agreement firm.

[tal-a04-v77] A teacher who obtained impressions elsewhere is directly Bhairava, because of scripture order and practice of that knowing teacher's wisdom.

[tal-a04-v78] Self-ascertained knowledge becomes Bhairava through fullness; it is stated from teacher, scripture, and self.

[tal-a04-v79] This knowledge has three sources; it shines through aggregate, inversion, and forms in night wandering.

[tal-a04-v80] Because of variety, instruments take axe, chisel, and saw to perform cutting.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-taddīkṣākramayogena śāstrārthaṃ vettyasau tataḥ / abhiṣekaṃ samāsādya yo bhavetsa tu kalpitaḥ sannapyaśeṣapāśaughavinivartanakovidaḥ / yo yathākramayogena kasmiṃścicchāstravastuni ākasmikaṃ brajedbodhaṃ kalpitākalpito hi saḥ / tasya yo@kalpito bhāgaḥ sa tu śreṣṭhamaḥ smṛtaḥ utkarṣaḥ śuddhavidyāṃśatāratamyakṛto yataḥ / yathā bhedenādisiddhācchivānmuktaśivā hyadhaḥ tathā sāṃsiddhikajñānādāhṛtajñānino@dhamāḥ / tatsaṃnidhau nādhikārasteṣāṃ muktaśivātmavat kiṃ tu tūṣṇīṃ-sthitiryadvā kṛtyaṃ tadanuvartanam / yastvakalpitarūpo@pi saṃvādadṛḍhatākṛte anyato labdhasaṃskāraḥ sa sākṣādbhairavo guruḥ / yataḥ śāstrakramāttajjñaguruprajñānuśīlanāt ātmapratyayitaṃ jñānaṃ pūrṇatvādbhairavāyate / tena śrīkiraṇoktaṃ yadgurutaḥ śāstrataḥ svataḥ tripratyayamidaṃ jñānamiti yacca niśāṭane / tatsaṃghātaviparyāsavigrahairbhāsate tathā karaṇasya vicitratvādvicitrāmeva tāṃ chidam / kartuṃ vāsīṃ ca ṭaṅkaṃ ca krakacaṃ cāpi gṛhṇate

chunks.l2:
[tal-a04-v81] Cutting is one from initial intention; thus the instrument's own body is to be spoken in measure.

[tal-a04-v82] Measure is not independent from self; attainment is not by force, and the knower's breath limit is said.

[tal-a04-v83] Breath is various from power descent; even in measure, measures have clear space.

[tal-a04-v84] Having seen, embraced, and chewed long with mind, the beloved satisfies them; what can we say to them?

[tal-a04-v85] Thus even in mental immersion, no path is attained; there is no futility, no infinite regress, and no mutual dependence.

[tal-a04-v86] Thus in yoga-limb inquiry, reasoning alone is not another inner means; it is for excellence of reflection.

[tal-a04-v87] The five restraints—non-harm, truth, non-stealing, celibacy, non-possession—are not useful in direct awareness.

[tal-a04-v88] Austerities and observances, posture, and breath control—all this is external manifestation.

[tal-a04-v89] In Viravali it was said: in awareness only, of Shiva-nature, by mind-dissolution bond, moon and sun are dissolved.

[tal-a04-v90] When the twelfth part is reached in the living sun, self-knowing liberation alone is declared; breath control is useless.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-tāvacca chedanaṃ hyekaṃ tathaivādyābhisaṃdhitaḥ / itthameva mitau vācyaṃ karaṇasya svakaṃ vapuḥ na svatantraṃ svato mānaṃ kuryādadhigamaṃ haṭhāt / pramātrāśvāsaparyanto yato@dhigama ucyate āśvāsaśca vicitro@sau śaktipātavaśāttathā / pramite@pi pramāṇānāmavakāśo@styataḥ sphuṭaḥ dṛṣṭvā dṛṣṭvā samāśliṣya ciraṃ saṃcarvya cetasā / priyā yaiḥ parituṣyeta kiṃ brūmaḥ kila tānprati itthaṃ ca mānasaṃplutyāmapi nādhigate gatiḥ / na vyarthatā nānavasthā nānyonyāśrayatāpi ca evaṃ yogāṅgamiyati tarka eva na cāparam / antarantaḥ parāmarśapāṭavātiśayāya saḥ ahiṃsā satyamasteyabrahmacaryāparigrahāḥ / iti pañca yamāḥ sākṣātsaṃvittau nopayoginaḥ tapaḥprabhṛtayo ye ca niyamā yattathāsanam / prāṇāyāmāśca ye sarvametadbāhyavijṛmbhitam śrīmadvīrāvalau coktaṃ bodhamātre śivātmake / cittapralayabandhena pralīne śaśibhāskare prāpte ca dvādaśe bhāge jīvāditye svabodhake / mokṣaḥ sa eva kathitaḥ prāṇāyāmo nirarthakaḥ

chunks.l2:
[tal-a04-v100] In self-reflection like the guru's word-reflection, when awakened — rejection of its opponents happens; in study-reflection it does not.

[tal-a04-v91] Breath control should not be done if it torments the body; one who knows the secret is liberated and is a liberator.

[tal-a04-v92] Withdrawal, named from objects and senses, indeed pins the unbound bond at its end.

[tal-a04-v93] Binding of mind in an object is concentration-natured; like-that knowledge continuity is meditation; supreme setting follows.

[tal-a04-v94] When objectness-identity alone arises in awareness, this absorption is emptiness of subject-object duality.

[tal-a04-v95] That triad of concentration, meditation, and absorption attains no use toward supreme awareness.

[tal-a04-v96] Yoga-limb status, from restraints to absorption, is described because of prior means and final reasoning use.

[tal-a04-v97] Rooted indeed within consciousness — through that, into breath and body, sowing in intellect by its practice; but this rule is not in consciousness.

[tal-a04-v98] Or, in our view, breath intellect body and the rest are clearly all-self — practice stationed there is removal of the other.

[tal-a04-v99] The body is made to leap from the essence of rising desire in leaping impact — by removing the dread of falling to the opposite side.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-prāṇāyāmo na kartavyaḥ śarīraṃ yena pīḍyate / rahasyaṃ vetti yo yatra sa muktaḥ sa ca mocakaḥ pratyāhāraśca nāmāyamarthebhyo@kṣadhiyāṃ hi yaḥ / anibaddhasya bandhasya tadantaḥ kila kīlanam cittasya viṣaye kvāpi bandhanaṃ dhāraṇātmakam / tatsadṛgjñānasaṃtāno dhyānamastamitā param yadā tu jñeyatādātmyameva saṃvidi jāyate / grāhyagrahaṇatādvaitaśūnyateyaṃ samāhitiḥ tadeṣā dhāraṇādhyānasamādhitritayī parām / saṃvidaṃ prati no kaṃcidupayogaṃ samaśnute yogāṅgatā yamādestu samādhyantasya varṇyate / svapūrvapūrvopāyatvādantyatarkopayogataḥ antaḥ saṃvidi rūḍhaṃ hi taddvārā prāṇadehayoḥ / buddhau vārpyaṃ tadabhyāsānnaiṣa nyāyastu saṃvidi atha vāsmaddṛśi prāṇadhīdehāderapi sphuṭam / sarvātmakatvāttatrastho@pyabhyāso@nyavyapohanam deha utplutisaṃpātadharmojjigamiṣārasāt / utplāvyate tadvipakṣapātāśaṅkāvyapohanāt guruvākyaparāmarśasadṛśe svavimarśane / prabuddhe tadvipakṣāṇāṃ vyudāsaḥ pāṭhacintane

chunks.l2:
[tal-a04-v101] Neither his knowledge nor word itself can the guru implant in intellect — therefore the self-awakening sequence is certain.

[tal-a04-v102] Therefore at dream-time, what is heard — even of that thing — identity-contemplation union is not for fruit, it is declared.

[tal-a04-v103] In disregard of convention, reflection fixed on word is the path; in regard for it, its meaning is thinking — let it be examined.

[tal-a04-v104] Practice in that non-dual consciousness is not useless — solely for uprooting the doubt of the duality-stain.

[tal-a04-v105] Duality-doubts are reasoned out by reasoning, it is stated — but for establishing that reasoning, even yama and the rest have instrumentality.

[tal-a04-v106] And in the former scripture it is said — neither duality nor non-duality — all liṅga-worship and the rest, beginning thus, by Shambhu.

[tal-a04-v107] All indeed is here prescribed, and even prohibited — yogas with prāṇāyāma and other limbs would be artificial, because.

[tal-a04-v108] By that, this uncreated is not worth a sixteenth part — but what here, O Goddess, is prescribed by rule?

[tal-a04-v109] The mind should be made steady in truth, and thus the supreme lord destroys dualistic reflection.

[tal-a04-v110] One situated in constant reflection on pure own-nature uses sense-objects as means.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-nahyasya guruṇā śakyaṃ svaṃ jñānaṃ śabda eva vā / dhiyi ropayituṃ tena svaprabodhakramo dhruvam ata eva svapnakāle śrute tatrāpi vastuni / tādātmyabhāvanāyogo na phalāya na bhaṇyate saṃketānādare śabdaniṣṭhamāmarśanaṃ paṭhiḥ / tadādare tadarthastu cinteti paricarcyatām tadadvayāyāṃ saṃvittāvabhyāso@nupayogavān / kevalaṃ dvaitamālinyaśaṅkānirmūlanāya saḥ dvaitaśaṅkāśca tarkeṇa tarkyanta iti varṇitam / tattarkasādhanāyāstu yamāderapyupāyatā uktaṃ śrīpūrvaśastre ca na dvaitaṃ nāpi cādvayam / liṅgapūjādikaṃ sarvamityupakramya śaṃbhunā vihitaṃ sarvamevātra pratiṣiddhamathāpi vā / prāṇāyāmādikairaṅgairyogāḥ syuḥ kṛttrimā yataḥ tattenākṛtakasyāsya kalāṃ nārghanti ṣoḍaśīm / kiṃ tvetadatra deveśi niyamena vidhīyate tattve cetaḥ sthiraṃ kāryaṃ tacca yasya yathāstviti / evaṃ dvaitaparāmarśanāśāya parameśvaraḥ kvacitsvabhāvamamalamāmṛśannaniśaṃ sthitaḥ / yaḥ svabhāvaparāmarśa indriyārthādyupāyataḥ

chunks.l2:
[tal-a04-v111] Without another facing it, conception arises by freedom in the self-luminous pure self.

[tal-a04-v112] In the flood of beings, the binder of difference is called night, but the self is the one range full of all meanings.

[tal-a04-v113] All this is pure knowledge; this conception is the clear form of pure knowledge.

[tal-a04-v114] Here reflection on pure knowledge destroys the mayic conception of difference in many ways.

[tal-a04-v115] By yoga of bathing, purity, worship, offering, meditation, chanting, etc., this universe is filled with the taste of self-awareness.

[tal-a04-v116] Having entered, the pure one should satisfy the whole path when the fire of awakening burns the fuel of the universe.

[tal-a04-v117] Immersion of the body in white ash is called bathing; thus bathing satisfies infinite deities.

[tal-a04-v118] Even from that, the body-beginning principles should be purified; even in these Shiva-nature principles, the distinguishing intellect is impurity.

[tal-a04-v119] That impurity is declared supreme; purity is crushing that intellect, so one's body becomes a vessel of awareness with dissolved difference.

[tal-a04-v120] Seeing mere awareness, the lord stands free; whatever is mind-pleasing arises wherever there is sense-station.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-vinaiva tanmukho@nyo vā svātantryāttadvikalpanam / tacca svacchasvatantrātmaratnanirbhāsini sphuṭam bhāvaughe bhedasaṃdhātṛ svātmano naiśamucyate / tadeva tu samastārthanirbharātmaikagocaram śuddhavidyātmakaṃ sarvamevedamahamityalam / idaṃ vikalpanaṃ śuddhavidyārūpaṃ sphuṭātmakam pratihantīha māyīyaṃ vikalpaṃ bhedabhāvakam / śuddhavidyāparāmarśo yaḥ sa eva tvanekadhā snānaśuddhyarcanāhomadhyānajapyādiyogataḥ / viśvametatsvasaṃvittirasanirbharitaṃ rasāt āviśya śuddho nikhilaṃ tarpayedadhvamaṇlam / ullāsibodhahutabhugdagdhaviśvendhanodite sitabhasmani dehasya majjanaṃ snānamucyate / itthaṃ ca vihitasnānastarpitānantadevataḥ tato@pi dehārambhīṇi tattvāni pariśodhayet / śivātmakeṣvapyeteṣu buddhiryā vyatirekiṇī saivāśuddhiḥ parākhyātā śuddhistaddhīvimardanam / evaṃ svadehaṃ bodhaikapātraṃ galitabhedakam paśyansaṃvittimātratve svatantre tiṣṭhati prabhuḥ / yatkiṃcinmānasāhlādi yatra kvāpīndriyasthitau

chunks.l2:
[tal-a04-v121] Worship is joined to brahman's true abode; indeed that worship is the union of separated beings.

[tal-a04-v122] Thus indeed by self-dependent pure infinite bhairavi consciousness, this consciousness is both inner and outer self.

[tal-a04-v123] From freedom, present reflective awareness itself is that; and all is included there in twelve ways.

[tal-a04-v124] The sun indeed is moon-self; that all-pervading established one is twelve-phase self, that consciousness in ultimate truth.

[tal-a04-v125] That shines always in mother knowledge, measure, instrument range, and object, taking fourfold form.

[tal-a04-v126] Pure consciousness, sound-form in eastern knowledge, is grasping-form in instrument because of yoga course.

[tal-a04-v127] O supreme lady, those in the white eye orb in direct perception have sixteen-spoked and twelve-spoked excellent wheels standing there.

[tal-a04-v128] Outside the red like elephant goad, those in black and white orbs are called second in the middle-going.

[tal-a04-v129] Dear one, those established inside, pure, shining like split ointment, are to be known in the four-petaled fire-moon nature.

[tal-a04-v130] O supreme lady, two wheels established in pairness mutually perform closing and opening.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-yojyate brahmasaddhāmni pūjopakaraṇaṃ hi tat / pūjā nāma vibhinnasya bhāvaughasyāpi saṃgatiḥ svatantravimalānantabhairavīyacidātmanā / tathāhi saṃvideveyamantarbāhyobhayātmanā svātantryādvartamānaiva parāmarśasvarūpiṇī / sa ca dvādaśadhā tatra sarvamantarbhavedyataḥ sūrya eva hi somātmā sa ca viśvamayaḥ sthitaḥ / kalādvādaśakātmaiva tatsaṃvitparamārthataḥ sā ca mātari vijñāne māne karaṇagocare / meye caturvidhaṃ bhāti rūpamāśritya sarvadā śuddhasaṃvinmayī prācye jñāne śabdanarūpiṇī / karaṇe grahaṇākārā yataḥ śrīyogasaṃcare ye cakṣurmaṇḍale śvete pratyakṣe parameśvari / ṣoḍaśāraṃ dvādaśāraṃ tatrasthaṃ cakramuttamam prativāraṇavadrakte tadbahirye taducyate / dvitīyaṃ madhyage ye te kṛṣṇaśvete ca maṇḍale tadantarye sthite śuddhe bhinnāñjanasamaprabhe / caturdale tu te jñeye agnīṣomātmake priye mithunatve sthite ye ca cakre dve parameśvari / saṃmīlanonmīlanaṃ te anyonyaṃ vidadhātake

chunks.l2:
[tal-a04-v131] As yoni and linga union flows immortal, so from immortal fire union they flow; no doubt.

[tal-a04-v132] From that wheel pressure at night light shines sun-moon going; seeing that supreme moonlight, time-knowledge proceeds.

[tal-a04-v133] The thousand-petaled wheel stands above those two, and from that wheel the cosmic egg arises, which is called that.

[tal-a04-v134] Standing there, the moon, kindled by fire, releases a stream and thus creates the entire endless world within itself.

[tal-a04-v135] Thus, in order, supreme nectar is everywhere in the wheels, from sixteen and twelve spokes to eight.

[tal-a04-v136] The moon flows as long as the path of five wheels; that is again drunk with delight by the shining swan, swan.

[tal-a04-v137] Once, by hearing, one is not stained by merit or sin, having become modified in the five-spoked wheel from the moon-flowing nectar.

[tal-a04-v138] The all-pervading one runs through the three-essence-spoked secret wheels, from which the world is born and dissolved by its own play.

[tal-a04-v139] There is bliss, and the celibate devotee devoted to that; there perfection and liberation are both attained equally.

[tal-a04-v140] Therefore one goes upward until the brahma-natured state, where fire and moon, equal, are created by self in self.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-yathā yoniśca liṅgaṃ ca saṃyogātsravato@mṛtam / tathāmṛtāgnisaṃyogāddravataste na saṃśayaḥ taccakrapīḍanādrātrau jyotirbhātyarkasomagam / tāṃ dṛṣṭvā paramāṃ jyotsnāṃ kālajñānaṃ pravartate sahasrāraṃ bhaveccakraṃ tābhyāmupari saṃsthitam / tataścakrātsamudbhūtaṃ brahmāṇḍaṃ tadudāhṛtam tatrasthāṃ muñcate dhārāṃ somo hyagnipradīpitaḥ / sṛjatītthaṃ jagatsarvamātmanyātmanyanantakam ṣoḍaśadvādaśārābhyāmaṣṭāreṣvatha sarvaśaḥ / evaṃ krameṇa sarvatra cakreṣvamṛtamuttamam somaḥ sravati yāvacca pañcānāṃ cakrapaddhatiḥ / tatpunaḥ pibati prītyā haṃso haṃsa iti sphuran sakṛdyasya tu saṃśrutyā puṇyapāpairna lipyate / pañcāre savikāro@tha bhūtvā somasrutāmṛtāt dhāvati trirasārāṇi guhyacakrāṇyasau vibhuḥ / yato jātaṃ jagallīnaṃ yatra ca svakalīlayā tatrānandaśca sarvasya brahmacārī ca tatparaḥ / tatra siddhiśca muktiśca samaṃ saṃprāpyate dvayam ata ūrdhvaṃ punaryāti yāvadbrahmātmakaṃ padam / agnīṣomau samau tatra sṛjyete cātmanātmani

chunks.l2:
[tal-a04-v141] The moon, heated and standing there, is placed in two calves; downward it drops fire-nectar, which flows in an instant.

[tal-a04-v142] Clearly, in ankles, knees, and so on, that curved sun-kindled power, heated again, creates the five-spoked and following order.

[tal-a04-v143] Thus it is to be known in the ear as well, from the toe up to the range of the foot-end and the vision of the cosmic egg.

[tal-a04-v144] Thus, not knowing, one is not a yogi; knowing, one becomes world-lord, and the supreme lord is seen by Brahma and others as a burning abode.

[tal-a04-v145] Here, by intent, the fourfold sequence is spoken in the eye; in each part, because of that, the twelve-natured description arises.

[tal-a04-v146] But the three-secret matter is not explained, because the goddess stands in measured form, shaped like a month cluster.

[tal-a04-v147] Therefore this consciousness is established as both inner and outer; shining by herself, she illuminates other things there.

[tal-a04-v148] Then this pure goddess, eager to manifest thus, considers creation; that scripture is called by that name.

[tal-a04-v149] Thus she, outward-facing, considers the partial coloring of illuminated things together with her own activity wheel, and enough from that too.

[tal-a04-v150] This very establishment of being, from the essence of inward-facing withdrawal, considering destruction of establishment, is called so.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-tatrasthastāpitaḥ somo dvedhā jaṅghe vyavasthitaḥ / adhastaṃ pātayedagniramṛtaṃ sravati kṣaṇāt gulphajānvādiṣu vyaktaṃ kuṭilārkapradīpitā / sā śaktistāpitā bhūyaḥ pañcārādikramaṃ sṛjet evaṃ śrotre@pi vijñeyaṃ yāvatpādāntagocaram / pādāṅguṣṭhātsamārabhya yāvadbrahmāṇḍadarśanam ityajānannaiva yogī jānanviśvaprabhurbhavet / jvalannivāsau brahmādyairdṛśyate parameśvaraḥ atra tātparyataḥ proktamakṣe kramacatuṣṭayam / ekaikatra yatastena dvādaśātmakatoditā na vyākhyātaṃ tu nirbhajya yato@tisarahasyakam / meye@pi devī tiṣṭhantī māsarāśyādirūpiṇī ata eṣā sthitā saṃvidantarbāhyobhayātmanā / svayaṃ nirbhāsya tatrānyadbhāsayantīva bhāsate tataśca prāgiyaṃ śuddhā tathābhāsanasotsukā / sṛṣṭiṃ kalayate devī tannāmnāgama ucyate tathā bhāsitavastvaṃśarañjanāṃ sā bahirmukhī / svavṛtticakreṇa samaṃ tato@pi kalayantyalam sthitireṣaiva bhāvasya tāmantarmukhatārasāt / saṃjihīrṣuḥ sthiternāśaṃ kalayantī nirucyate

chunks.l2:
[tal-a04-v151] From that too, in the full essence of dissolution, she herself produces self-natured, obstacle-making doubt in part, and also withdraws.

[tal-a04-v152] Having withdrawn doubt except its doubtable meaning, in the being-circle she indeed considers withdrawal, from dissolving in her own self-fire.

[tal-a04-v153] And that dissolving-natured being-withdrawal is indeed touched in the self, by which this may shine as swallowed by me.

[tal-a04-v154] The withdrawable condition of this is indeed the own nature of consciousness; in purified, conditionless consciousness-form it is established.

[tal-a04-v155] Even when the being-flood is dissolved, she then makes some being sticky; doubt indeed remains in impression-form.

[tal-a04-v156] By auspicious and inauspiciousness, this will be born with fruit-abundance, before or after enjoyment; this doubt stands apart.

[tal-a04-v157] Even what is congealed elsewhere is dissolved by consciousness itself, like rites dissolve grave acts.

[tal-a04-v158] Consciousness discerns form through constriction and dissolution, dissolving and then congealing again.

[tal-a04-v159] When something enjoyable is enjoyed, consciousness withdraws its instruments and discerns twelve in the self.

[tal-a04-v160] The group of action, intellect, and senses is twelvefold and expands in distinct objects because of its illuminating sun-nature.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-tato@pi saṃhārarase pūrṇe vighnakarīṃ svayam / śaṅkāṃ yamātmikāṃ bhāge sūte saṃharate@pi ca saṃhṛtya śaṅkāṃ śaṅkyārthavarjaṃ vā bhāvamaṇḍale / saṃhṛtiṃ kalayatyeva svātmavahnau vilāpanāt vilāpanātmikāṃ tāṃ ca bhāvasaṃhṛtimātmani / āmṛśatyeva yenaiṣā mayā grastamiti sphuret saṃhāryopādhiretasyāḥ svasvabhāvo hi saṃvidaḥ / nirupādhini saṃśuddhe saṃvidrūpeṣastamīyate vilāpite@pi bhāvaughe kaṃcidbhāvaṃ tadaiva sā / āśyānayedya evāste śaṅkā saṃskārarūpakaḥ śubhāśubhatayā so@yaṃ soṣyate phalasaṃpadam / pūrvaṃ hi bhogātpaścādvā śaṅkeyaṃ vyavatiṣṭhate anyadāśyānitamapi tadaiva drāvayediyam / prāyaścittādikarmabhyo brahmahatyādikarmavat rodhanāddrāvaṇādrūpamitthaṃ kalayate citiḥ / tadapi drāvayedeva tadapyāśyānayedatha itthaṃ bhogye@pi saṃbhukte sati tatkaraṇānyapi / saṃharantī kalayate dvādaśaivāhamātmani karmabuddhyakṣavargo hi buddhyanto dvādaśātmakaḥ / prakāśakatvātsūryātmā bhinne vastuni jṛmbhate

chunks.l2:
[tal-a04-v161] Ego is the instrument of pride and dissolves through uninterrupted reflection.

[tal-a04-v162] As differentiated instruments like sword and noose dissolve into the undifferentiated hand, so this rule holds.

[tal-a04-v163] The goddess of consciousness freely discerns the flood of senses as a sun-disk in the imagined ego-self.

[tal-a04-v164] That supreme sun, full and thirteenfold, clearly dissolves in the agent because of its instrumentality.

[tal-a04-v165] The agent is said to be twofold, imagined and unimagined; the imagined one is discussed through body-intellect distinction.

[tal-a04-v166] In scriptures time-fire-rudra is defined; time joined with distinction is remembered as fire-enjoyer.

[tal-a04-v167] Through samsara's made and unmade states, the lord constrains and dissolves, and ego dissolves while bound being remains.

[tal-a04-v168] He too, because of imagined function, dissolves in 'I am this' in great expanding time.

[tal-a04-v169] In this self-knowledge, consciousness shines with a blossoming form.

[tal-a04-v170] Though full, consciousness dissolves in its abode.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-ahaṃkārastu karaṇamabhimānaikasādhanam / avicchinnaparāmarśī līyate tena tatra saḥ yathāhi khaṅgapāśādeḥ karaṇasya vibhedinaḥ / abhedini svahastādau layastadvadayaṃ vidhiḥ tenendriyaughamārtaṇḍamaṇḍalaṃ kalayetsvayam / saṃviddevī svatantratvātkalpite@haṃkṛtātmani sa eva paramādityaḥ pūrṇakalpastrayodaśaḥ / karaṇatvātprayātyeva kartari pralayaṃ sphuṭam kartā ca dvividhaḥ proktaḥ kalpitākalpitātmakaḥ / kalpito dehabuddhyādivyavacchedena carcitaḥ kālāgnirudrasaṃjñāsya śāstreṣu paribhāṣitā / kālo vyavacchittadyukto vahnirbhoktā yataḥ smṛtaḥ saṃsārāklṛptiklṛptibhyāṃ rodhanāddrāvaṇātprabhuḥ / anivṛttapaśūbhāvastatrāhaṃkṛtpralīyate so@pi kalpitavṛttitvādviśvābhedaikaśālini / vikāsini mahākāle līyate@hamidaṃmaye etasyāṃ svātmasaṃvittāvidaṃ sarvamahaṃ vibhuḥ / iti pravikasadrūpā saṃvittiravabhāsate tato@ntaḥsthitasarvātmabhāvabhogoparāgiṇī / paripūrṇāpi saṃvittirakule dhāmni līyate

chunks.l2:
[tal-a04-v171] All this here is consciousness only.

[tal-a04-v172] The supreme lady has unconditioned free will.

[tal-a04-v173] These imaginings are projection, knowledge, enumeration, movement, and sound.

[tal-a04-v174] Projection divides the self; knowledge is the undifferentiated of the divided.

[tal-a04-v175] Movement ascends to own form; sound is the remainder of self-reflection.

[tal-a04-v176] The supreme goddess performs the fivefold imagination.

[tal-a04-v177] Knower-ness becomes clear in knowers.

[tal-a04-v178] Consciousness stands twelvefold in world-mothers.

[tal-a04-v179] There is no fixed order.

[tal-a04-v180] The pure consciousness principle operates anywhere.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-pramātṛvargo mānaughaḥ pramāśca bahudhā sthitāḥ / meyaugha iti yatsarvamatra cinmātrameva tat iyatīṃ rūpavaicitrīmāśrayantyāḥ svasaṃvidaḥ / svācchandyamanapekṣaṃ yatsā parā parameśvarī imāḥ prāguktakalanāstadvijṛmbhocyate yataḥ / kṣepo jñānaṃ ca saṃkhyānaṃ gatirnāda iti kramāt svātmano bhedanaṃ kṣepo bheditasyāvikalpanam / jñānaṃ vikalpaḥ saṃkhyānamanyato vyatibhedanāt gatiḥ svarūpārohitvaṃ pratibimbavadeva yat / nādaḥ svātmaparāmarśaśeṣatā tadvilopanāt iti pañcavidhāmenāṃ kalanāṃ kurvatī parā / devī kālī tathā kālakarṣiṇī ceti kathyate mātṛsadbhāvasaṃjñāsyāstenoktā yatpramātṛṣu / etāvadantasaṃvittau pramātṛtvaṃ sphuṭībhavet vāmeśvarīti-śabdena proktā śrīniśisaṃcare / itthaṃ dvādaśadhā saṃvittiṣṭhantī viśvamātṛṣu ekaiveti na ko@pyasyāḥ kramasya niyamaḥ kvacit / kramābhāvānna yugapattadabhāvātkramo@pi na kramākramakathātītaṃ saṃvittattvaṃ sunirmalam / tadasyāḥ saṃvido devyā yatra kvāpi pravartanam

chunks.l2:
[tal-a04-v181] There worship is already whole, because the resonance that arises of itself is nothing but self-reflection.

[tal-a04-v182] That ever-arising self-reflection is called the supreme, great heart; seated in the heart, it has melted the whole universe.

[tal-a04-v183] Scripture gives it the common name spanda: the current running from the first grasp of a state to its end, rising in the self.

[tal-a04-v184] This slight stirring, this shimmer of nothing else, is the wave on the ocean of awakening, never present without consciousness.

[tal-a04-v185] Ocean-ness is a movement where waves are never two; the essence of all this is consciousness, while the inert is only the world.

[tal-a04-v186] Because everything rests on it, that essence is the great heart, the root of brahman named the egg of māyā.

[tal-a04-v187] Will, knowledge and action are never truly named apart from their ascent, and that ascent is the threefold power rising in the consciousness-self of Bhairavī.

[tal-a04-v188] What is released from that, and set outside, is released once more; thus their true form is the self of the threefold power.

[tal-a04-v189] Drawing the emission back by supreme knowledge, it goes on; that alone, wearing an outer form, is burnt away in the fire of prior knowing.

[tal-a04-v190] The inner-sounding reflection is left as residue, and that is already enough: void-selfhood itself is reached from beyond the range of the three powers.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-tatra tādātmyayogena pūjā pūrṇaiva vartate / parāmarśasvabhāvatvādetasyā yaḥ svayaṃ dhvaniḥ sadoditaḥ sa evoktaḥ paramaṃ hṛdayaṃ mahat / hṛdaye svavimarśo@sau drāvitāśeṣaviśvakaḥ bhāvagrahādiparyantabhāvī sāmānyasaṃjñakaḥ / spandaḥ sa kathyate śāstre svātmanyucchalanātmakaḥ kiṃciccalanametāvadananyasphuraṇaṃ hi yat / ūrmireṣā vibodhābdherna saṃvidanayā vinā nistaraṅgataraṅgādivṛttireva hi sindhutā / sārametatsamastasya yaccitsāraṃ jaḍaṃ jagat tadadhīnapratiṣṭhatvāttatsāraṃ hṛdayaṃ mahat / tathā hi sadidaṃ brahmamūlaṃ māyāṇḍasaṃjñitam icchājñānakriyārohaṃ vinā naiva saducyate / tacchaktitritayārohādbhairavīye cidātmani visṛjyate hi tattasmādbahirvātha visṛjyate / evaṃ sadrūpataivaiṣāṃ satāṃ śaktitrayātmatām visargaṃ parabodhena samākṣipyaiva vartate / tatsadeva bahīrūpaṃ prāgbodhāgnivilāpitam antarnadatparāmarśaśeṣībhūtaṃ tato@pyalam / khātmatvameva saṃprāptaṃ śaktitritayagocarāt

chunks.l2:
[tal-a04-v191] Becoming feeling-nature, it melts into the self of dissolution; this is the heart of destruction, and in creation the heart's own thought.

[tal-a04-v192] This natural, unobstructed self-reflection, they say, is 'I', and it is nothing but the luminosity of light.

[tal-a04-v193] For this power indeed is the heart-essence of all mantras — without it they would be inert, like the living without a heart.

[tal-a04-v194] Risen in this unartificial heart, whatever one does — by breath or reflection — all of it is held to be his japa.

[tal-a04-v195] Whatever is created by own will, from creation-nature outward and inward — that indeed is his ultimate meditation.

[tal-a04-v196] For in formless consciousness-light, all-form-containing — for fruit-desirers some form remains as meditation-object.

[tal-a04-v197] As from non-difference, in full being, one bringing water — abandoning other acts — seeks the pot, from essence.

[tal-a04-v198] So indeed from the supreme Lord's fixed-order unfolding, some form produces some fruit-conception.

[tal-a04-v199] But he who is full-hearted and desires neither fruit nor name — his is the world-forming goddess, by abandonment of limitation.

[tal-a04-v200] In kula, of the yogin whirling from supreme Bhairava-wine — stability in the body, whatever seal that is, is mudra.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-vedanātmakatāmetya saṃhārātmani līyate / idaṃ saṃhārahṛdayaṃ prācyaṃ sṛṣṭau ca hṛnmatam etadrūpaparāmarśamakṛtrimamanābilam / ahamityāhureṣaiva prakāśasya prakāśatā etadvīryaṃ hi sarveṣāṃ mantrāṇāṃ hṛdayātmakam / vinānena jaḍāste syurjīvā iva vinā hṛdā akṛtrimaitaddhṛdayārūḍho yatkiṃcidācaret / prāṇyādvā mṛśate vāpi sa sarvo@sya japo mataḥ yadeva svecchayā sṛṣṭisvābhāvyādbahirantarā / nirmīyate tadevāsya dhyānaṃ syātpāramārthikam nirākāre hi ciddhāmni viśvākṛtimaye sati / phalārthināṃ kācideva dhyeyatvenākṛtiḥ sthitā yathā hyabhedātpūrṇe@pi bhāve jalamupāharan / anyākṛtyapahānena ghaṭamarthayate rasāt tathaiva parameśānaniyatipravijṛmbhaṇāt / kācidevākṛtiḥ kāṃcit sūte phalavikalpanām yastu saṃpūrṇahṛdayo na phalaṃ nāma vāñchati / tasya viśvākṛtirdevī sā cāvacchedavarjanāt kule yogina udriktabhairavīyaparāsavāt / ghūrṇitasya sthitirdehe mudrā yā kācideva sā

chunks.l2:
[tal-a04-v201] Without regard for inner fuel-provision, constantly — blazing, its fierce flame spread over floods of eyes, the fire.

[tal-a04-v202] In such knowledge-fire, beings entering — raising his true glory — attain the causality of sacrifice-acts.

[tal-a04-v203] Whosoever, purified by the supreme Lord's power-descent, manifested before — let him stand himself; as said, he is initiated.

[tal-a04-v204] From japa through homa, though in each single rite supreme custom arises — nevertheless thus it is determined.

[tal-a04-v205] Just as a horse driven in a painted land with equal lows and highs goes along a path imagined by mere wish.

[tal-a04-v206] So, through the varied patterns of consciousness, peaceful, fierce, and the rest, duality is abandoned and becomes Bhairava.

[tal-a04-v207] Just as, perceiving one's own face in a mirror placed before one, one again knows that same face as one's own self.

[tal-a04-v208] So, in the mind-mirror of meditation, worship, and ritual, seeing oneself as Bhairava, one soon becomes identified with him.

[tal-a04-v209] Becoming identified is the attainment in the supreme self; it is the supreme limit of fullness, and here there is no other fruit.

[tal-a04-v210] All fruit is imagined in incompleteness, there and there; but in unimagined fullness, what other fruit could be spoken?
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-antarindhanasaṃbhāramanapekṣyaiva nityaśaḥ / jājvalītyakhilākṣaughaprasṛtograśikhaḥ śikhī bodhāgnau tādṛśe bhāvā viśantastasya sanmahaḥ / udrecayanto gacchanti homakarmanimittatām yaṃ kaṃcitparameśānaśaktipātapavitritam / purobhāvya svayaṃ tiṣṭheduktavaddīkṣitastu saḥ japyādau homaparyante yadyapyekaikakarmaṇi / udeti rūḍhiḥ paramā tathāpītthaṃ nirūpitam yathāhi tatra tatrāśvaḥ samanimnonnatādiṣu / citre deśe vāhyamāno yātīcchāmātrakalpitām tathā saṃvidvicitrābhiḥ śāntaghoratarādibhiḥ / bhaṅgībhirabhito dvaitaṃ tyājitā bhairavāyate yathā puraḥsthe mukure nijaṃ vaktraṃ vibhāvayan / bhūyo bhūyastadekātma vaktraṃ vetti nijātmanaḥ tathā vikalpamukure dhyānapūjārcanātmani / ātmānaṃ bhairavaṃ paśyannacirāttanmayībhavet tanmayībhavanaṃ nāma prāptiḥ sānuttarātmani / pūrṇatvasya parā kāṣṭhā setyatra na phalāntaram phalaṃ sarvamapūrṇatve tatra tatra prakalpitam / akalpite hi pūrṇatve phalamanyatkimucyatām

chunks.l2:
[tal-a04-v211] This sacrifice rite exists in someone's heart, and it pleases the wheel of consciousness quickly after birth.

[tal-a04-v212] In this sacrifice one attains isolation, though seen by people while standing in the body-bond rite.

[tal-a04-v213] Here the lord stated conduct in the eighteenth chapter: there is neither purity nor impurity, nor consideration of food and the like.

[tal-a04-v214] Neither duality nor non-duality; neither linga worship and the like, nor abandonment of that, nor non-possession or possession.

[tal-a04-v215] Possession, or collection of matted hair, ash, and the like, and abandonment of that, are not determined by performance or nonperformance of vows.

[tal-a04-v216] Entry into fields and the like, observance of vows and the like, other forms, lingas, names, clans, and the like are not essential here.

[tal-a04-v217] Here nothing is prescribed and nothing is prohibited; even what is prescribed is also prohibited.

[tal-a04-v218] But what is prescribed here, O goddess? The mind must be steadied in truth by a very serene yogin.

[tal-a04-v219] He should act accordingly as it is for him; with mind steady in truth, even while enjoying sense objects.

[tal-a04-v220] He is not touched by faults, like a lotus leaf by water, even while eating, protected by poison-removing mantra and the like.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-eṣa yāgavidhiḥ ko@pi kasyāpi hṛdi vartate / yasya prasīdecciccakraṃ drāgapaścimajanmanaḥ atra yāge gato rūḍhiṃ kaivalyamadhigacchati / lokairālokyamāno hi dehabandhavidhau sthitaḥ atra nāthaḥ samācāraṃ paṭale@ṣṭādaśe@bhyadhāt / nātra śuddhirna cāśuddhirna bhakṣyādivicāraṇam na dvaitaṃ nāpi cādvaitaṃ liṅgapūjādikaṃ na ca / na cāpi tatparityāgo niṣparigrahatāpi vā saparigrahatā vāpi jaṭābhasmādisaṃgrahaḥ / tattyāgo na vratādīnāṃ caraṇācaraṇaṃ ca yat kṣetrādisaṃpraveśaśca samayādiprapālanam / parasvarūpaliṅgādi nāmagotrādikaṃ ca yat nāsminvidhīyate kiṃcinna cāpi pratiṣidhyate / vihitaṃ sarvamevātra pratiṣiddhamathāpi ca kiṃ tvetadatra deveśi niyamena vidhīyate / tattve cetaḥ sthirīkāryaṃ suprasannena yoginā tacca yasya yathaiva syātsa tathaiva samācaret / tattve niścalacittastu bhuñjāno viṣayānapi na saṃspṛśyeta doṣaiḥ sa padmapatramivāmbhasā / viṣāpahārimantrādisaṃnaddho bhakṣayannapi

chunks.l2:
[tal-a04-v221] Poison does not delude him; likewise the great-minded yogin. How indeed could the body and so forth, made of five elements, be called impure?

[tal-a04-v222] Beyond luminosity, what purity or impurity of a thing? And would the purity of an impure state be only such?

[tal-a04-v223] Thus here earth would be purified from water and water from earth, a mutual dependence that is futile and leads to infinite regress.

[tal-a04-v224] This mutual dependence, even in impurity, makes the order futile: impure water would purify earth and vice versa.

[tal-a04-v225] From air water, from fire air, or from elsewhere; many-formed mantras are purifiers, and purity arises in them.

[tal-a04-v226] If mantras are pure by nature, why then Shiva-nature? If purity is in them, why is that needed there too?

[tal-a04-v227] Non-recognition of Shiva-nature is not in mantras as in earth; if they are pure by that, then cognition of purity is purity itself.

[tal-a04-v228] For the yogi that purity exists in things; indeed, by injunction the determination of pure, impure, and so forth is made.

[tal-a04-v229] Let it be so; even so, what injunction spoken by Shiva would be true if this is elsewhere?

[tal-a04-v230] If this is overruled by the Vedic, would the opposite not become true, if you think correctly, from specific objectness?
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-viṣaṃ na muhyate tena tadvadyogī mahāmatiḥ / aśuddhaṃ hi kathaṃ nāma dehādyaṃ pāñcabhautikam prakāśatātirikte kiṃ śuddhyaśuddhī hi vastunaḥ / aśuddhasya ca bhāvasya śuddhiḥ syāttādṛśaiva kim anyonyāśrayavaiyarthyānavasthā itthamatra hi / pṛthivī jalataḥ śuddhyejjalaṃ dharaṇitastathā anyonyāśrayatā seyamaśuddhatve@pyayaṃ kramaḥ / aśuddhājjalataḥ śuddhyeddhareti vyarthatā bhavet vāyuto vāriṇo vāyostejasastasya vānyataḥ / bahurūpādikā mantrāḥ pāvanātteṣu śuddhatā mantrāḥ svabhāvataḥ śuddhā yadi te@pi na kiṃ tathā / śivātmatā teṣu śuddhiryadi tatrāpi sā na kim śivātmatvāparijñānaṃ na mantreṣu dharādivat / te tena śuddhā iti cettajjñaptistarhi śuddhatā yoginaṃ prati sā cāsti bhāveṣviti viśuddhatā / nanu codanayā śuddhyaśuddhyādikaviniścayaḥ itthamastu tathāpyeṣā codanaiva śivoditā / kā syātsatīti cedetadanyatra pravitānitam vaidikyā bādhiteyaṃ cedviparītaṃ na kiṃ bhavet / samyakcenmanyase bādho viśiṣṭaviṣayatvataḥ

chunks.l2:
[tal-a04-v231] By exception it is to be done in a general injunction; purity and impurity in a general injunction, in truth-teaching.

[tal-a04-v232] When man is overruled, thus it is described here; and no doubt about arthavada etc. would be in the Maheshvara sentence.

[tal-a04-v233] Without prior intelligence, thus established, doubt toward false meaning would always be in scripture of sky-form etc.

[tal-a04-v234] God, full of unlimited consciousness and universal form, standing as scripture-self, does not deserve falsity anywhere.

[tal-a04-v235] As desiring being-form, as the Lord wishing to stand, by naming its own form, wishing to stand, he thus stands.

[tal-a04-v236] Even arthavada, where it sees other injunction etc., there let it be untrue; in freedom he indeed is enjoiner.

[tal-a04-v237] In another injunction sentence, going to auxiliary state or not, this indeed is not meaningless, like elephant etc. from proximity.

[tal-a04-v238] Its self-meaning shines by self-awareness only; denial of that is possible in injunction and prohibition.

[tal-a04-v239] And reason is here in sentences, self-awareness also unoverruled, which makes certainty of whole meaning gem truth.

[tal-a04-v240] In dead body then, body-born, which impurity is declared; elsewhere not thus; let them understand impure, fallen from consciousness.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-apavādena kartavyaḥ sāmānyavihite vidhau / śuddhyaśuddhī ca sāmānyavihite tattvabodhini puṃsi te bādhite eva tathā cātreti varṇitam / nārthavādādiśaṅkā ca vākye māheśvare bhavet abuddhipūrvaṃ hi tathā saṃsthite satataṃ bhavet / vyomādirūpe nigame śaṅkā mithyārthatāṃ prati anavacchinnavijñānavaiśvarūpyasunirbharaḥ / śāstrātmanā sthito devo mithyātvaṃ kvāpi nārhati icchāvānbhāvarūpeṇa yathā tiṣṭhāsurīśvaraḥ / tatsvarūpābhidhānena tiṣṭhāsuḥ sa tathā sthitaḥ arthavādo@pi yatrānyavidhyādimukhamīkṣate / tatrāstvasatyaḥ svātantrye sa eva tu vidhāyakaḥ vidhivākyāntare gacchannaṅgabhāvamathāpi vā / na nirarthakaṃ evāyaṃ saṃnidhergajaḍādivat svārthapratyāyanaṃ cāsya svasaṃvittyaiva bhāsate / tadapahnavanaṃ kartuṃ śakyaṃ vidhiniṣedhayoḥ yuktiścātrāsti vākyeṣu svasaṃviccāpyabādhitā / yā samagrārthamāṇikyatattvaniścayakāriṇī mṛtadehe@tha dehotthe yā cāśuddhiḥ prakīrtitā / anyatra neti buddhyantāmaśuddhaṃ saṃvidaścyutam

chunks.l2:
[tal-a04-v241] All attains consciousness-identity — pure thence, established; and in the glorious Vira-row, in pure-impure discernment, it is said.

[tal-a04-v242] The living is the carrier of all — nothing is non-living; whatever is lifeless is impure — know that.

[tal-a04-v243] Therefore what is not too far from consciousness would bring purity — by a non-conceptual state even sages thus became.

[tal-a04-v244] But for world-protection that principle was concealed by them — though outer things exist, purity and impurity are not like blue.

[tal-a04-v245] This indeed is cognizer-dharma, from experiencing consciousness as one and not-one — or if even object-nature, bound to measure-dependence.

[tal-a04-v246] In the Sautramani liquor is pure for the hotr — for another's pure things, reversal; by this, injunctions too are contradicted by his own words.

[tal-a04-v247] As sometimes shown, like brahmahatya injunction-prohibition — food-rules too, relying on this reasoning, are practiced.

[tal-a04-v248] And at the supreme-knowledge beginning the Great Lord speaks indeed — what sages gods Brahma Visnu Rudra and the rest declared.

[tal-a04-v249] By increasing superiority overcoming prior upon prior — the Shaiva is never to be refuted by Vaishnava words.

[tal-a04-v250] The Vishnu-related should be discussed through Brahma-born and the rest — who obstructs from perversity is deluded and becomes sin's sharer.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-saṃvittādātmyamāpannaṃ sarvaṃ śuddhamataḥ sthitam / śrīmadvīrāvalau coktaṃ śuddhyaśuddhinirūpaṇe sarveṣāṃ vāhako jīvo nāsti kiṃcidajīvakam / yatkiṃcijjīvarahitamaśuddhaṃ tadvijānata tasmādyatsaṃvido nātidūre tacchudvimāvahet / avikalpena bhāvena munayo@pi tathābhavan lokasaṃrakṣaṇārthaṃ tu tattattvaṃ taiḥ pragopitam / bahiḥ satsvapi bhāveṣu śuddhyaśuddhī na nīlavat pramātṛdharma evāyaṃ cidaikyānaikyavedanāt / yadi vā vastudharmo@pi mātrapekṣānibandhanaḥ sautrāmaṇyāṃ surā hotuḥ śuddhānyasya viparyayaḥ / anena codanānāṃ ca svavākyairapi bādhanam kvacitsaṃdarśitaṃ brahmahatyāvidhiniṣedhavat / bhakṣyādividhayo@pyenaṃ nyāyamāśritya carcitāḥ sarvajñānottarādau ca bhāṣate sma maheśvaraḥ / nararṣidevadruhiṇaviṣṇurudrādyudīritam uttarottaravaiśiṣṭyāt pūrvapūrvaprabādhakam / na śaivaṃ vaiṣṇavairvākyairbādhanīyaṃ kadācana vaiṣṇavaṃ brahmasaṃbhūtairnetyādi paricarcayet / bādhate yo vaiparītyātsamūḍhaḥ pāpabhāgbhavet

chunks.l2:
[tal-a04-v251] Therefore primarily, Skanda, do not practice worldly dharmas — and not what other scriptures prescribe; in your own, practice what the stream declares.

[tal-a04-v252] From which — though by God even the Veda was established — nevertheless indeed from the contraction-presence-absence alternative...

[tal-a04-v253] Bound knowledge is declared by contraction, while lordly knowledge by expansion is obstructive.

[tal-a04-v254] This duality is not so; how can maya-made difference be non-imagined?

[tal-a04-v255] In the bharga crest, death-time arts arising from duality options are swallowed.

[tal-a04-v256] In doctrine, linga worship states world-path embodiment; in kula contexts it is forbidden for body world-self embodiment.

[tal-a04-v257] Here, in all-self, why is that rule prohibited by rule entry for identity realization?

[tal-a04-v258] In kula, matted hair etc is abandoned by easy means; vow practice serves mantra-meaning identity.

[tal-a04-v259] Its prohibition serves mantra universal-self realization; entry into fields and seats serves obstacle peace.

[tal-a04-v260] For the mantra worshipper's gain, the rule of not going to fields etc is taught for own self.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-tasmānmukhyatayā skanda lokadharmānna cācaret / nānyaśāstrasamuddiṣṭaṃ srotasyuktaṃ nije caret yato yadyapi devena vedādyapi nirūpitam / tathāpi kila saṃkocabhāvābhāvavikalpataḥ saṃkocatāratamyena pāśavaṃ jñānamīritam / vikāsatāratamyena patijñānaṃ tu bādhakam idaṃ dvaitamidaṃ neti parasparaniṣedhataḥ / māyīyabhedaklṛptaṃ tatsyādakālpanike katham uktaṃ bhargaśikhāyāṃ ca mṛtyukālakalādikam / dvaitādvaitavikalpotthaṃ grasate kṛtadhīriti siddhānte liṅgapūjoktā viśvādhvamayatāvide / kulādiṣu niṣiddhāsau dehe viśvātmatāvide iha sarvātmake kasmāttadvidhipratiṣedhane / niyamānupraveśena tādātmyapratipattaye jaṭādi kaule tyāgo@sya sukhopāyopadeśataḥ / vratacaryā ca mantrārthatādātmyapratipattaye tanniṣedhastu mantrārthasārvātmyapratipattaye / kṣetrapīṭhopapīṭheṣu praveśo vighnaśāntaye mantrādyārādhakasyātha tallābhāyopadiśyate / kṣetrādigamanābhāvavidhistu svātmanastathā

chunks.l2:
[tal-a04-v261] Fullness by universal form is described to know; conventional practice existence is taught as to be protected.

[tal-a04-v262] By difference as life, abandoning each purifies principle; convention prohibition is said in doctrinal scriptures.

[tal-a04-v263] Let boundless complete self-awakening be understood; this form is another's, but my own is to be meditated.

[tal-a04-v264] Flame linga belongs to another, but skull etc is my own; etc includes asceticism and hospitality.

[tal-a04-v265] Named with Sakti-Siva as extremes — this is mine, not otherwise; and lineage, guru-continuum, called mathika-kula.

[tal-a04-v266] Srisamtati named Tryambaka, called half-destruction — thus here half-four mathikas, in the Sankara order.

[tal-a04-v267] By yuga-sequence the siddha-continuum from Kurma to Fish — and by the word beginning: house, village, pithas and sub-pithas.

[tal-a04-v268] Mudra is the kiss, and their self-other-situated procedure — for identity-realization indeed resort to your own continuum.

[tal-a04-v269] Enjoy, worship the wheel — but not indeed through another's tormentor; and this is forbidden in mata-treatises, since it is refutation.

[tal-a04-v270] Even in the undivided supreme reality, by this difference it arises — thus field-entry and the rest, from the continuity-rule's end.

[tal-a04-v271] In this it is not enjoined — indeed not directly suitable in Shiva; nor is it prohibited — for that would break that very principle.

[tal-a04-v272] Of the universal-self Lord indeed, in his own form, injunction and prohibition are imagined — in power, not in breaking own-nature.

[tal-a04-v273] But in entry into supreme reality, whatever near means one knows when — it is to be accepted then, to be abandoned then, or sometimes.

[tal-a04-v274] No constraint is to be made here, it is said in Sri-Trika teaching — equality of all gods, of creeper-mantra-letters.

[tal-a04-v275] Of arrivals and goings all is Shiva-filled — for he beholds undivided true being, the Shiva-principle.

[tal-a04-v276] Who approaches undivided true-being as self-principle — in ketaki-flower fragrance intensely the bee is connoisseur, not the fly; in supreme nondual Bhairava worship someone delights, impelled by Mahesa.

[tal-a04-v277] For those resting in this yoga, worldly pomp dissolves by itself, like snow in great summer.

[tal-a04-v278] Enough of excessive digression in this overly expanded matter: Abhinavagupta too is fit in the sacrifice rite, O wise one.

[tal-a04-v279] In the manifestation of the supreme word, the Shakta means is distinct today.
